context.description: McLaren Vale is a wine region about 40 minutes south of Adelaide, with around 80 cellar doors spread over hills and vineyards. Its coast runs for 31 km along Gulf St Vincent, from the cliffs of Maslin Beach to the wide sands at Aldinga and Sellicks. Willunga, the region's slate-built township, has galleries and a courthouse museum, while the d'Arenberg Cube sits on a hilltop among the vines.

context.description: Victor Harbor is a seaside town on Encounter Bay on the southern Fleurieu coast, built around a foreshore and the causeway to Granite Island. A horse-drawn tram crosses the causeway to the island, where little penguins breed and a walking trail circles the coast. Southern right whales come close to shore in winter, and the town has a whale centre and a free clifftop platform on the Heysen Trail. The sheltered bay at Port Elliot and the Bluff headland are a short drive east and west.

context.description: Goolwa sits on the lower Murray where the river meets Lake Alexandrina, a few kilometres from the Southern Ocean. A series of barrages holds back the sea, and you can walk halfway across the Goolwa Barrage. The wharf precinct has an interpretive centre on the Murray Mouth, and a bridge leads to Hindmarsh Island and its waterbirds. A surf beach runs south-east of town, and Strathalbyn and Langhorne Creek are an easy drive inland.

context.description: Yankalilla is a farming town about 73 km south of Adelaide, set among rolling hills with the Bungala River running through it. The district reaches west to the beaches of Normanville and Carrickalinga and south to the bush and cliffs of Deep Creek National Park. Cape Jervis, at the peninsula's western tip, is the Kangaroo Island ferry gateway. The 85 km Hills and Seascapes Discovery Drive links many of the district's landscapes.
